new_statements.quote: [p.124] ... syllabe longue. Ailleurs l'accent est sur la première syllabe. Mais cinq formes canoniques (des disyllabes) échappent à cette règle : certains lexèmes appartenant à ces formes ont effectivement l'accent sur la première syl[labe] ... [p.125] 8.31. L'accent a trois fonctions en arabe babalia : – redondante : pour une syllabe longue accentuée c'est la longueur qui est pertinente, l'accent est un trait obligatoire mais non pertinent ; démarcative : c'est ce qui se passe l'accent est sur la première syllabe ... ; distinctive : dans certaines oppositions la place de l'accent est en effet le seul trait distinctif. [p.126] ... syllabe accentuée est toujours la plus haute.
new_statements.translation: [p.124] ... long syllable. Elsewhere the accent is on the first syllable. But five canonical forms (disyllables) escape this rule: some lexemes belonging to these forms do have the accent on the first syllable ... [p.125] 8.31. The accent has three functions in Babalia Arabic: – redundant: for an accented long syllable it is length that is distinctive, the accent being an obligatory but non-distinctive feature; demarcative: this is what happens [when] the accent is on the first syllable ...; distinctive: in certain oppositions the position of the accent is in fact the only distinctive feature. [p.126] ... the accented syllable is always the highest [in pitch].

new_statements.rule_in_words: In the lexical word, the accent falls on the long (CV:) syllable when there is one; otherwise it falls on the first syllable. Five disyllabic canonical forms escape this rule: in them accent placement is lexically contrastive (minimal pairs dura 'grain' vs du'ra 'arm'; hekka 'he scratches' vs hekka 'he scratched', p. 125). The accent is realised as pitch — the accented syllable is always the highest — which Décobert attributes to the Berakou (tonal) substrate; his 1985 monograph reopens the question ('Accent, hauteur ou ton ?') and a 1992 summary calls it 'un accent de hauteur mélodique et non un accent d'intensité'.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Not mentioned in the snippets seen.
new_statements.exceptions: Five disyllabic canonical forms where accent position alone distinguishes lexemes (dura/du'ra, hekka/hekka type pairs); monosyllables explicitly left aside (8.29 'Nous n'évoquons pas les monosyllabes'); 1985: loanwords (French toit, etc.) do not always show pitch tied to length; the pitch-height list is admitted not to be 'parfaitement cohérente' (p. 126).
new_statements.domain_note: Word level: 'accent des unités lexicales', stated over the canonical forms of lexemes (citation forms); the GLECS summary also distinguishes a phrase accent, not visible here.
new_statements.identity_note: baba1273 is a retired/spurious languoid (ISO CR 2019-013, effective 2020-01-23). The variety Décobert describes is the Chadian Arabic (chad1249; ISO shu) spoken in the Babalia villages of the Bas-Chari (Bût al-Fîl area below Goulfei) by an ethnic group shifting from Berakou (bera1261; ISO bxv, retired) to Arabic; the 'creole' label comes from Décobert's p. 127 remark that one may speak of a 'créolisation' of Arabic in Babalia country (an Arabic lexicon marked by the African substrate). If catalogued, file as a dialect record under chad1249 ('Babalia dialect of Chadian Arabic, Décobert 1977'), not as a separate language; note that Décobert's 'accent' is pitch-realised and partly lexically contrastive, so the entry may belong in a pitch accent/tonal-with-stress bin depending on the 1985 monograph.

sources.note: Sec. 8.28-8.31 'L'accent des unités lexicales' pp. 124-126: accent placement is the problem; the accent is on the long syllable, 'ailleurs l'accent est sur la première syllabe'; five disyllabic canonical forms escape the rule and show minimal pairs by accent placement (dura 'graine' / du'ra 'bras'; hekka 'il gratte' / hekka 'il a gratté'); accent has three functions (redundant with length, demarcative on first syllable, distinctive); the accented syllable is always the highest in pitch, a 'nature tonale de l'accent' attributed to Berakou substrate (p. 126-127). Snippets only, not full pages.
